Read the vendor page of each record. State the price per TB-month, the egress rule and the identity kind. Choose paid-only or a qualifying verdict when the host sells capacity; keep fails-quota only with a quoted reason that names a capacity or price shortfall against the 10 TiB stored / 1 TiB a day served need.
An audit of the first attempt judged these claims unsupported by their sources; settle each one first:
- storage/koofr $.egress.terms: the tier limits are right (200 GB, 1 TB, 4 TB daily public transfer), but the derived figure is wrong: a 4 TB daily limit on the 5 TB Crate plan is about 120 TB a month, not ~30 TB/mo; the free plan has a 50 GB daily public limit, not mentioned
- storage/hostbrr-storagebox $.interface: neither the comparison page nor the Storagebox page names rclone; SSH, FTP, FTPS and rsync are stated, SFTP is only implied (the comparison page says tools can already talk FTP, SFTP, or rSync); rclone would work only through its sftp or ftp backend, which is an inference, not a statement
- storage/hostbrr-storagebox $.interface: the no-S3 part is supported, but the value lists rclone, which neither page names; SFTP is only implied by SSH access
